summary_en: K891, backed by Hikari Tsushin (34%), MBK Partners (33%), and NEC Capital Solutions (33%), completed a tender offer for Leopalace21 on October 30, 2026. K891 will acquire 100% of Leopalace21's shares through the completed offer, while Hikari Tsushin will transition K891 to an equity-method affiliate post-closing.
title_en: Notice Regarding the Results of the Tender Offer for the Common Stock and Subscription Rights to New Shares of Leopalace21 Inc. Made by K891 Inc., a Subsidiary as of the Commencement of the Tender Offer, and Changes in Subsidiaries (Affiliate Status)
translation_en_brief:
K891 Inc., initially a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hikari Tsushin, commenced a tender offer for all common shares and subscription rights to new shares of Leopalace21 Inc. (TSE Prime Market, code 8848) on September 15, 2026. The tender offer concluded on October 30, 2026, with K891 acquiring 100% of Leopalace21's securities.

Following the completion, K891's ownership structure is being reorganized. Hikari Tsushin, MBK Partners, and NEC Capital Solutions will jointly own K891's parent company K892 with shareholdings of 34%, 33%, and 33% respectively. Under this new structure, Leopalace21 will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of K891, which in turn will be held by the consortium through K892. The transaction is financed in part by LBO loans of up to 236 billion yen.

Post-closing, K891 will cease to be a subsidiary of Hikari Tsushin and will be reclassified as an affiliate accounted for under the equity method. Leopalace21 will not be consolidated into Hikari Tsushin's financial statements; instead, Hikari Tsushin's share of K892's results will be reflected as equity-method investment income. The transaction strengthens Leopalace21's operations through collaboration among the three co-investors while maintaining Hikari Tsushin's strategic involvement.
